title: Impact of Short-Form Videos on Screentime and Sleep: Evidence from TikTok
eligible_reason: All reported estimates come from a stacked (Cengiz et al. style) design with matched not-yet-treated controls: the analysis file is a stacked weekly panel with 68 adoption-week stacks (panel_week), the fixed effects are panelist x stack (panelist_group = panelist_id-panel_week) and calendar week x stack (week_group = week-panel_week), and controls are matched later adopters (type = notyettreated_panelists, with a matching subclass). Stacked DiD and matching-based designs are excluded by the protocol.
design_notes: Treatment: first TikTok use (first_tt_week, 95 distinct adoption weeks among the panelists in the file). Within each stack, after = 1 for treated panelists in weeks rel >= 0. Regressions (Code.R lines 277, 350, 449, 517, 579, 644, 753): feols(y ~ after | panelist_group + week_group, data = stacked_panel_sleep_matched filtered to n_bin == l) with clustering by panelist; Figure 6 uses i(rel, ref = -1) event-time dummies with the same stacked FE. Every model is run separately by TikTok-usage intensity bin (n_bin 1-3; sample splits). Outcomes: screen_time, non_tt_screen_time, category minutes, pickups, tot_sleep, tot_sleep_hr, tot_wake_hr, hour-of-day screen time. Table 5 regresses sleep on TikTok minutes (continuous). Controls in each stack are not-yet-treated adopters (all panelists in the file have a first_tt_week), so there are no never-treated units. An unstacked TWFE could in principle be constructed from panelist_id x week with first_tt_week, but that is not what the paper reports.

ineligible_main_text_specs.reason: stacked event study with panelist x stack and week x stack FE, matched controls
stacked static DiD, matched controls, split by usage bin

n_adoption_cohorts_note: 68 stacks (panel_week) in Final panel.csv; 95 distinct first_tt_week values across treated and control panelists
data_files_note: data/Final panel.csv (117,792 rows: 58,896 treated and 58,896 not-yet-treated control panelist-weeks, 68 stacks) plus seven small CSVs for descriptive figures; underlying device-level panel is proprietary (Above Data).
software_detail: R 4.5.1, fixest 0.13.2; single script code/Code.R; run log Code_run_log.html
screener_notes: Design is staggered adoption in substance, but the published estimator is a matched stacked DiD (cites Cengiz et al. 2019, Baker et al. 2022, Goodman-Bacon 2021, Callaway-Sant'Anna 2021 per full-text flags), which falls outside the protocol. The prepared stacked panel is in the package if the team ever wants an unstacked re-analysis, but there would be no published TWFE counterpart.
